issues.description: The template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with signature addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) while the problem statement (UML and textual description) and the solution both expect addGuestStudents(int). This parameter mismatch will prevent students from implementing and testing the intended method signature and will cause compilation/test failures or confusion when students implement addGuestStudents(int) as required by the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template method signature to match the specification and solution: change the method to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). Alternatively, provide an overload public void addGuestStudents(int) that delegates to the existing method, but the simplest fix is to remove the boolean parameter so the template matches the UML and solution.

issues.description: The template's Lecture.addGuestStudents method signature includes an extra boolean parameter (validateInput) while the problem statement UML and the solution implementation define addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch in the method signature (extra parameter name) breaks the direct mapping from the exercise description to the starter code and reference solution and may confuse students about the intended API and how to implement or call the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template method signature with the UML and solution by changing the template stub to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } (remove the boolean validateInput parameter) or update the problem statement and solution to document and require the boolean parameter if intentional.
